ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure compares two sets of population data from 2000 and 2010. In 2000, the province's permanent resident population was 82.35 million, the natural population growth rate was 0.51%, and the proportion of urban population was 27%; in 2010, the permanent resident population was 80.42 million, the natural population growth rate was 0.23%, and the proportion of urban population was 40%. It can be seen that over the ten years, the permanent resident population decreased, but the natural population growth rate was still a positive value. Then reason: The question stem states that in recent years the national natural population growth rate has been about 0.5%. The province's natural growth rate in 2010 was lower than the national level, but it was still not negative growth, indicating that the birth population was still greater than the death population, and the decrease in permanent resident population cannot mainly be attributed to negative natural growth. Permanent resident population refers to the population that actually lives in the local area for more than half a year. If a large number of people leave this province to work elsewhere and live there for more than half a year, they are no longer counted in this province's permanent resident population. Combined with the characteristic that western provinces in China have relatively many people going out for work, the main reason for the decrease in permanent resident population should be the increase in the number of labor service exports, leading to net population out-migration.
